doors.trait: Letting people in stopped being something you decline and became something you cannot quite locate. Fine, you say, on the day of the diagnosis, the layoff, the breakup. The word has three hundred uses now, and not one of them means fine.
doors.scene: On the day of the diagnosis you said fine. Layoff, fine. Breakup, fine. The word has become a door painted to look like a wall, and the people who love you have quietly stopped testing whether it opens.
doors.outside: The people close to you have learned to read your weather at a distance, because asking gets them fine. They compare notes about you. They worry in committee, exactly the way you trained them to, and call it respecting your space.
